subject.title: refactor(agents): shared spawn orchestration pipeline behind backend adapters

question: Should the agent-runtime owner accept the unified registration and lifecycle boundary after reviewing redacted real native and ACP spawn evidence for the current head?
rationale: The protected maintainer label and the deliberately different backend session-key and failure contracts require owner judgment; static checks cannot establish that the shared ordering preserves both runtime behaviors.

options.title: Require two-backend runtime proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until it includes redacted after-fix native and ACP spawn output or logs showing successful registration, progress, and completion or cleanup behavior.

options.title: Accept the test-only evidence
options.body: An agent-runtime owner may accept the refactor based on the focused test suite and completed CI lanes, explicitly taking responsibility for the remaining live-equivalence uncertainty.

recommendation.title: Require two-backend runtime proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until it includes redacted after-fix native and ACP spawn output or logs showing successful registration, progress, and completion or cleanup behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch history shows direct ownership of the shared pipeline and its backend-contract follow-up fixes.
